summary: The five-member Commission of Inquiry was sworn in on Thursday 30 July before Chief Magistrate Judy Latchman, in the presence of President Irfaan Ali; Chairman Justice Godfrey Philip Smith took his oath virtually. "The media were not invited to the event that was held in the presence of President Irfaan Ali. Questions have been raised publicly about the impartiality of a number of the inquirers." "The Secretary to the commission has not yet been named." — the first direct statement in the corpus on the secretary qu

This is the first OFFICIAL statement of the Commission's statutory basis: "The CoI was established under Section 2(1) of the Commissions of Inquiry Act, Chapter 19:03, to investigate the circumstances surrounding the capsizing and sinking of the MV Barima, owned and operated by the Transport and Harbours Department, on the night of July 18, 2026." The oath was administered by Chief Magistrate Judy Latchman at State House, Georgetown; Justice Smith participated virtually.

Four commissioners took the oath in person at State House; Chairman Justice Godfrey Phillip Smith was administered the oath virtually by Chief Magistrate Judy Latchman. "The ceremony was not open to media but was streamed on the President's social media pages." — this is the only account explaining how the event was made public. Ali described the commissioners as "persons of exceptional professional standing" and said the nation deserves "a full, fair and impartial account of what occurred, why it occurred."

"The five-member panel was appointed by the President under the Commissions of Inquiry Act." Kiskadee reported the same statutory basis on 27 July; it is now corroborated by DPI. "The President also mentioned that the commissioners would determine their own procedures and conduct the inquiry independently" — the only report in the corpus that the Commission sets its own procedure. "Justice Smith, who was not yet in Guyana, took his oath virtually, while the other commissioners were sworn in in person."

The five-member Commission was sworn in on Thursday 30 July, with President Ali "vowing that the government would support the work of the body." Ali: "Our nation deserves a full, fair and impartial account of what occurred, why it occurred and what must be done to ensure that such a tragedy is never repeated. The government will provide administrative, technical and financial support necessary. Every resource required will be made available."

This is the first record in the corpus of the Attorney General personally defending the murder charges and characterising the accused. It is a serious escalation and the archive holds nothing like it. Attorney General Anil Nandlall is reported to have said that "accounts indicate the captain was under the influence of alcohol and narcotics." This is an unproven allegation by a member of the Executive about a named accused person who has not been tried, made while the matter is before the court. It is recorded here

Nandlall: opposition legislators "have exploited people's anger, they have exploited people's trauma, they have exploited people's pain." Nandlall characterises Monday's National Assembly sitting as "converted into an indecent vulgar melee" rather than reflecting the solemnity a national tragedy demands. "Opposition Leader Azruddin Mohamed and Parliamentary group leader Terrence Campbell were each offered time to express condolences but refused, instead continuing protest activities." This is the first item in the corpus that squarely touches claims, limitation and legal representation of the families. It is a direct answer to the archive's compensation gap. Opposition Leader Azruddin Mohamed "announced plans to assemble a legal team to advise families of victims from the MV Barima tragedy, urging them to refrain from signing compensation paperwork without legal counsel." Mohamed: "I will have a legal team to represent them to ensure that they are handsomely compensated."

MOST IMPORTANT NEW FACT OF RECORD: the charge particulars are published for the first time — "The indictable charge alleges that on 18th July, 2026, at a point 9.3 nautical miles on a bearing of 040° off the Essequibo Coast at Devonshire Castle, the trio murdered 72 named victims." The 72 victims are NAMED in the charge. This is the first explanation in the corpus of how the number 72 is constituted. This closes the archive's flagged gap: the APA picket of 29 July, previously recorded ONLY from two social-media posts, is now carried in the domestic press. The picket took place "Wednesday morning" (29 July) outside the Office of the President on Vlissengen Road and was "attended by roughly 100 people, including civil society groups, political parties, and relatives of victims." Chants: "Edghill and Indar Must Go" and "Indigenous Lives Matter."

First press record of a THIRD protest site: "Family members and staff of the Transport and Harbours Department protested across Demerara on Wednesday" — at Den Amstel (WCD), at Melanie Damishana (ECD), and outside the Office of the President. At Den Amstel "approximately 30 demonstrators gathered"; they "chanted 'jail the criminals, free the innocent' and held placards reading 'wrongly accused, wrongly judged' and 'free Delon Granderson'."

Confirms the 3 August Charity Magistrate's Court date is UNCHANGED as at 30 July: "The three accused remain on remand pending their next court appearance on August 3 at the Charity Magistrate's Court." No bail application, no further charge, no variation is reported anywhere in this survey. Transparency Institute of Guyana Inc. (TIGI) President Mike Singh publicly questions the impartiality of members of the Commission on the day they are sworn in. Singh: "This arbitrary arrest, slapping of murder charges upon the lower ranks, the operational crew for the Barima—this itself defeats the whole purpose of any such Commission of Inquiry. Based on the evidence submitted and the findings of the Commission of Inquiry, only then could you move towards instituting any types of charges."

ENTIRELY NEW TO THE RECORD: the Ministry of Public Works has, for the first time, published an itemised list of its own consigned cargo aboard the MV Barima on the fatal voyage. The Ministry's statement, quoted: "Please be advised, the Ministry of Public Works wishes to inform the public that the consigned cargo aboard the MV Barima, on the Ministry's behalf, at the time of the July 18 Departure, is as follows." The list is: "One Honda Side-by-Side ATV"; "Six Drums of Gasoline"; "Four Drums of Diesel."

Crowd size given as "Over a hundred demonstrators" outside the Office of the President on 29 July — larger than Kaieteur's "roughly 100." Jean La Rose on the wreck: "It carries a lot of information. It carries a lot of evidence. It carries souls of the people. It must be raised so our people can have closure." Placards recorded: "Indigenous Voices Matter", "Stop treating our first people as an afterthought", "Edghill must Gooo!", "We deserve safe passage home", "Safe passage is a right not a privilege."

FIGURE OF RECORD ON PAYMENTS: "On Tuesday, Poon said she received $350,000 from the Government to assist with funeral expenses." The archive carried APNU's 25 July complaint that some families were offered "a mere $300,000"; this is a first-person account of an actual payment, at a different figure, on 28 July. Louvicia Poon, 30, of Wakenaam lost her 11-year-old son Ronaldo and her 17-year-old brother Christian Rodrigues. Poon: "I had to accept what I got. I can't really understand this government."

Chief Engineer Paul Seepersaud, 44, a T&HD employee with "more than three decades at sea", was buried on Wednesday 29 July at the Wesleyan Church, New Amsterdam. [SINGLE SOURCE — identification detail] "Seepersaud's body was recovered on July 20… His sister told Kaieteur News that she identified him by the distinctive tattoos on his body." Dickson: "We were really impressed with the efforts on the ground… The Ministry of Health is doing so much on the ground in Region One." "Where there is evidence suggesting negligence or breaches of legal duty, the affected families should be encouraged to seek independent legal advice regarding the filing of civil lawsuits against any individuals, agencies, or entities that may bear legal responsibility."

"According to news reports of Saturday, 73 bodies have been recovered and 76 rescued. Taking the official count of 179 passengers on board the MV Barima, it means that 30 of them are still unaccounted for." Lall does the same arithmetic the archive does and reaches the same place. "Over a week after the disaster, there is still uncertainty about how many passengers, paying or not, with a ticket or lacking one, were onboard the vessel."
